 FOOTBALL International Football Armando la ‘Hormiga’ González is challenging Rafael Márquez’s decision to bench him
 Mexico failed to win any of Rafa Márquez's first four games as coach
 Mexico's Armando Gonzalez controls the ball during the World Cup Group A soccer match between Mexico and South Africa in Mexico City. 
 JORGE GORDILLO

 SOCCER Mauricio Pochettino, new manager of Manchester United
 Rafael Márquez’s start as head coach of the Mexican National Team has tested the patience of fans and analysts alike ahead of his first official competitive fixture. Stepping into the top job following the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the legendary former captain oversaw a winless four-game friendly run this autumn.
 After settling for back-to-back 1-1 draws against Colombia and Peru in September, El Tri suffered consecutive shutout losses in October, falling 3-0 to the United States and 2-0 to Chile . The lack of finishing in the final third has emerged as the squad’s biggest flaw, Mexico’s attackers went 270 straight minutes without finding the net across their last three outings.
 Mexico gives Julián Quiñones a hero's farewell after historic World Cup Now, as the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals kick off this FIFA international break against Jamaica , beginning Saturday, November 14 in Kingston before the return leg in Monterrey on November 17, Márquez urgently needs his frontline to produce with a Final Four spot and direct qualification to the 2027 Gold Cup on the line.
 Why Armando “Hormiga” González Should Start  Against Jamaica
 With veteran striker Raúl Jiménez sidelined through injury, reports out of Mexico’s training camp indicate Márquez is leaning toward giving Santiago Giménez the starting nod in Kingston, a choice that has sparked widespread debate among supporters.
 While Giménez brings high-profile European experience, Armando “Hormiga” González arrives at the November camp in far sharper form. Focusing on the three core arguments for making the switch, elevating González into the starting XI over Giménez stands out as the smartest tactical move for El Tri:
 Superior Club Scoring Rhythm : González joins the national team from Olympiacos riding a strong run of form, tallying five goals and two assists so far this campaign. Conversely, Giménez has struggled to find consistent rhythm and clinical finishing at FC Porto , recording just two goals and one assist across eight official appearances this season.
 Investing in the 2030 World Cup Cycle : With the national program already shifting its long-term focus toward the 2030 FIFA World Cup , González represents the natural generational spearhead for Mexico’s attack. Given his age, upward trajectory, and current sharpness, handing him high-pressure competitive minutes in Kingston aligns directly with Márquez’s mandate to build for the next four-year cycle.
 Rewarding Meritocracy Inside the Locker Room : Granting starting roles to players performing at their peak sends an unmistakable message of accountability across the roster. After earning his European move from Chivas and immediately delivering results abroad, choosing González over a veteran enduring a prolonged international goal drought, Giménez has scored just six goals in 51 senior appearances , with none since September 2025 , reinforces competitive merit within the squad.
 Regardless of who Márquez chooses for this game, Mexico must show its potential and make its presence felt. Otherwise, Márquez could choose someone else for the second leg.
